title: OTLP resume and compatibility prober for flaky backend exporters
creator: Asha Patel
description: Implement an OTLP exporter wrapper that can detect transient backend failures (e.g., Tempo/Jaeger endpoints or third-party collectors), resume in-flight streams with idempotent replay where supported, and run lightweight schema/compatibility probes before switching exporters. The goal is to reduce trace loss during short outages and avoid misrouting caused by incompatible backend schemas after upgrades.
acceptance_criteria: When the configured tracing backend returns 5xx or connection resets for < 2 minutes, the exporter wrapper buffers minimally and transparently retries with exponential backoff without dropping parent spans

If the backend advertises a schema mismatch (proto/gRPC incompatibility or OTLP resource attribute mismatch) the wrapper runs a compatibility probe and switches to configured fallback exporter variant (eg. tempo-legacy-shim) with audit log
Idempotent replay ensures duplicate detection for span IDs within a 5-minute window when backend performs dedup på its side, documented with metrics for duplicates and replays
End-to-end tests simulate collector restarts and confirm <1% trace loss for short outages in our CI harness
Console shows per-tenant exporter health, last-compatibility-probe timestamp, and replay counts as part of observability UI
design_summary: Add an exporter-side resiliency layer that sits between the SDK tracer and concrete OTLP exporter. The layer maintains a small durable buffer (memory-backed with optional ephemeral file fallback), a state machine (healthy, degraded, probing, failing-over) and a compatibility probe module that performs a small synthetic OTLP request using the same resource attributes and headers to validate schema/semantic compatibility. For backends that support stream resume (gRPC bidirectional or server-side replay tokens), surface resume tokens and attach them to retried streams. Metrics: exporter_health{tenant, backend}, replay_count, duplicate_detected_count, probe_latency_ms. Configuration surface: buffer_size_bytes, max_inflight_spans, probe_interval_ms, fallback_exporter_key, replay_window_seconds. Implementation will be in Rust to reuse existing runtime codepaths and keep low-latency hot paths.
rollout_plan: 1) Feature flag behind runtime-observability.resilient-exporter. 2) Canary rollout to internal staging tenants (5% of ingestion) for 48h with increased sampling. 3) Monitor replay_count, exporter_health, and end-to-end latency. 4) Expand to early customers (opt-in) for a week. 5) Full rollout to hosted OTLP endpoints after no regressions for two weeks.
testing_plan: Unit tests for state machine transitions and probe responses. Integration tests: simulated Tempo/Jaeger with induced schema change and restart sequences in CI using local fake-collector. Load test: 1000 rps tracing traffic with 10k span/s sustained to ensure backpressure and buffer eviction behave. Chaos test: randomly terminate backend for 30–90s and verify <1% trace loss and stable latencies. Add e2e smoke that validates console metrics surface and alert triggers.
